published_statement: No published statement exists for the census datum as the tree uses it (unsourced). The physics the row actually computes with is the ideal-conductor Casimir result E/A = -pi^2 hbar c/(720 d^3) (Casimir 1948; NAMED-NOT-READ this stage), whose validity condition the tree itself states: 'Perfect-conductor idealisation needs the gap to exceed the plate material's plasma wavelength' (scale.py:142-143; same condition at index3.py:711 and README.md:3994).
published_hypotheses: H1 (Casimir 1948 ideal result, as restated in the tree at scale.py:142-143 and tolman.py:1318-1321): perfectly conducting parallel plates, i.e. gap d >> plate plasma wavelength lambda_p (gold lambda_p = 137.8 nm, tolman.py:1511; hbar omega_p = 9.0 eV, tolman.py:1142).
H2: T = 0, infinite flat plates, vacuum gap, continuum (macroscopic electrodynamics) description of the plates -- requires d well above interatomic spacing.
H3 (the census, unsourced): 10 nm is the smallest separation reached by 'state of the art' Casimir apparatus; 0.1 nm is an 'atomic floor' below which no gap exists.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1 at achievable.py:134-135 and 417-419 (casimir_density docstring 'The measured effect'): the ideal perfect-conductor density is applied at d = 10 nm and 0.1 nm, both below gold's lambda_p = 137.8 nm, and labelled 'MEASURED effect'. The tree's own scale.py:142-143 states the formula needs d > lambda_p. Computed here (T=0 Lifshitz, gold plasma model, hbar omega_p = 9.0 eV): E_real/E_ideal = 0.1099 at 10 nm (Drude gamma=35 meV: 0.1093), 0.525 at 100 nm, 0.919 at 1 um. So at 10 nm the printed density is ~9.1x above what real gold gives; the label 'MEASURED' is inaccurate at these gaps (the measured force tracks the ideal formula only for d >> lambda_p).

DROPPED H2 at achievable.py:127, 135, 534: 0.1 nm is below gold's fcc nearest-neighbour distance 0.288 nm (named constant, a = 0.4078 nm), i.e. below atomic contact; no continuum Casimir/Lifshitz energy exists there. The row uses a formula outside its domain; 'atomic floor' is a generous bound (smaller than any physical vacuum gap), not a measured apparatus.

WEAKENED status of H3 at achievable.py:126-127 / 533-534: 'state of the art' carries no source and no date; the owner's own tag 'CENSUS claim ... not a theorem' (achievable.py:138-139, 547) is accurate but the census row is unsourced -- per M's rules it is DECLARED, not READ.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis applied here: did the row's authors lack data? The owner lacked (or did not use) one datum it itself holds elsewhere -- the plasma wavelength of the plate material. tolman.py:1142/1511 cites gold hbar omega_p = 9.0 eV and lambda_p = 137.8 nm, and scale.py:142-143 states the ideal formula needs d > lambda_p, yet achievable.py:134-135/417-419 applies the ideal formula at 10 nm and 0.1 nm and calls it MEASURED. Having that datum in the row changes the NUMBERS (10 nm corridor x3.02 larger; 0.1 nm row outside any continuum theory) but NOT the conclusion: evidence is the computed eta = 0.1099 < 1 and b_real > b_ideal at every gap -- the real Casimir energy at sub-lambda_p gaps is weaker than the ideal formula, never stronger. Evidence the other way (that a missing datum could rescue the apparatus): none found; no material makes the Lifshitz energy exceed the perfect-conductor value between identical plates (|r| <= 1 in every term, which the integrator makes explicit), so the ideal row is an upper bound on the plate-configuration density at fixed d. The census datum itself ('10 nm state of the art') could not be read this stage and remains OPEN; it is not claimed stale or wrong.
grade_evidence: NARROWED, not WRONG and not STANDS. The formula the row computes with (ideal perfect-conductor Casimir density) holds on a smaller class (d >> lambda_p ~ 138 nm for gold) than the tree uses (d = 10 nm and 0.1 nm) -- a hypothesis the tree drops at achievable.py:134-135 and 417-419 while stating it at scale.py:142-143. Computed here: at 10 nm real gold gives 0.1099 of the ideal density (Drude 0.1093), so the 'MEASURED effect' label is inaccurate by ~9x at that gap; at 0.1 nm the gap is below atomic contact (0.288 nm) and no continuum result applies. The drift is in the SAFE direction: every correction increases the required corridor (10 nm: 6.455e20 -> 1.948e21 m), so the row's conclusion 'This is not an engineering programme' is strengthened, not weakened; this is recorded as a discrepancy of label and domain, not a refutation. The tree's own arithmetic (b, ly, 72.951, 8.541, 7.6e19/7.6e15, 8630 AU core) reproduces exactly. SEPARATELY OPEN: the census datum '10 nm state of the art' has no source in the owner and none could be READ here (alphaXiv quota exceeded; arXiv and publisher sites egress-blocked); search summaries (van Zwol 2008: transition ~10% lambda_p; SFA Au data above 8.5 nm) are consistent with ~10 nm as the edge of measured metal-metal dispersion forces but are not a READ and are not quoted as one.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner relabels casimir_density as the ideal perfect-conductor UPPER BOUND on the plate density (not 'the measured effect') at d < lambda_p and flags the 0.1 nm row as outside continuum validity, AND a READ source (e.g. arXiv:0902.4022 or 0809.1779) dates the ~10 nm census. To OPEN for the whole entry: if one holds that the census datum, not the formula, is the result under audit -- it remains unread. To WRONG: only a computed case in which real plates at d = 10 nm give a LARGER energy density than the ideal formula (none exists for identical passive plates, |r| <= 1), or a READ source showing Casimir-regime apparatus far below 10 nm that shrinks the corridor below the tree's printed figures -- neither found.
